I have farmed these 10 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. I finished primary school and that is all — everything else I learned from my father and from watching what happens in the field. This year I will keep 8.1 mu for the wheat-maize rotation and 2 mu for cotton, same as last year. I am not changing that because my neighbor Lao Wang switched his cotton all to maize two years ago and the price fell, so he lost money. Change is risky.

For the winter wheat, after the maize comes off in early June, I will run the rotary tiller twice to make a fine seedbed for October sowing. I buy improved Jimai seed from the county dealer. For fertilizer I put down one full bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer — that is 50 jin per mu — as base, and then in March I topdress with half a bag of urea, 25 jin per mu. That is about 19 jin of nitrogen per mu, same as last year, and I am not cutting it because the wheat price is steady and I cannot afford a thin ear. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the seedlings do not freeze, once at jointing, and once at heading. I spray twice — herbicide for weeds at the three-leaf stage, and one insecticide if aphids show up. If the spring rain is normal I expect about 550 kilos per mu.

For summer maize there is no time to plow after wheat harvest — I hire the no-tillage planter to put the hybrid seed straight into the stubble. At sowing I spread 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu, and when the plants are knee-high I add 20 jin of urea per mu. That is about 16 or 17 jin of nitrogen per mu. I irrigate two times, at the big trumpet stage and during grain filling. Two pesticide sprays: one herbicide right after sowing, and one for corn borer when I see moths. I hope for 600 kilos per mu.

For the 2 mu of cotton, I deep-plow in April because cotton roots need loose soil. I plant hybrid Bt cotton seed — the bag costs more but I save on bug spray later. I put down 50 jin of 15-15-15 per mu as base, then add 30 jin of urea, half at flowering and half at boll stage. That is about 21 jin of nitrogen per mu. Cotton drinks more water, so I irrigate three times. Even though the seed is Bt, I still spray four times this year — I heard bollworm is getting stronger, and I would rather spend 80 yuan on spray than lose the bolls. I expect about 350 kilos of seed cotton per mu.

Money is tight. My son works in Shijiazhuang and sends some back, but a bag of urea is over 120 yuan now. Still, I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. A bag of fertilizer wasted is just money; a bad harvest is a disaster. I do the work with my wife, and I hire Lao Li for two days at wheat harvest and maybe one day at cotton picking. The well pump is old but it works — I just watch the electricity bill.
